Hyderabad rains: Roads flooded, Zepto rider rescued from nala
Residents have been asked to plan their travel accordingly.
News Desk Follow on Twitter |   Edited by Saleha Fatima  |   Published: 30th October 2026 6:06 pm IST|   Updated: 30th October 2026 9:30 pm IST
Zepto rider rescued from nala amid heavy rains in Hyderabad
Hyderabad: Hyderabad saw heavy rains on Friday, October 30, leading to waterlogging and heavy traffic on major routes. While the rains have largely subised, more spells are expected overnight, according to local weather enthusiast T Balaji.
Keesara received the highest rainfall in the Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri recording 108.8 mm, according to the Telangana Development Planning Society.
This was followed by Bahadurpura at 82.3 mm and Madhapur at 73.5 mm.
Zepto rider rescued from nala
A 46-year-old Zepto delivery executive, identified as Ghantasala Arjun Kumar, accidentally entered a nala along with his bike near Vital Rao Nagar due to the heavy flow of water at around 7:30 pm, police said.
He was promptly rescued by the police and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams. His bike is yet to be retrieved.
A 46-year-old Zepto delivery executive had a narrow escape on Friday evening after he accidentally fell into a nala along with his bike near Vittal Rao Nagar, as heavy water flow swept him in.

Waterlogging
Waterlogging was reported at Pillar No 117 and Pillar No 196 at PVNR Expressway resulting in slow vehicular movement. The Monsoon Emergency Teams are on-site monitoring the situation.

Slow vehicular movement has been reported at Tippu Khan Bridge, Bapu Ghat towards Langar Houz.

Slow traffic movement is also reported at Malakunta Road towards Gandhi Bhavan. Several other routes are also severely waterlogged. Residents can monitor traffic updates on the X handles of Hyderabad Traffic Police and plan their travel accordingly.
Rains till November 4
Balaji has also predicted moderate to heavy rains in east Telangana between November 2 and 4.
The rest of the state will get light to moderate rains for the next five to six days.
